I do HEMA and we sometimes do blunt-weapon sparring in public parks, so I actually had to deal with that question in the past.

Long story short, check local possession laws for bladed weapons, talk to the police and make sure they know what you're doing and where you're doing it, and when the police tells you not to do something - don't do it. For us it wasn't a problem (talked to city hall to explain our deal to them, got permission to carry training weapons in the park, had to show them our security measures so no bystanders would walk into us and get hit), but I actually know guys who were explicitly forbidden to carry sparring swords and spears in public.

I can understand cops getting upset if you're carrying a sword or spear like you're ready to use it, but why should they care if you're just walking along with it? Even Carson City let you keep your guns.

Less than half a year ago some guy in my city used a "vicious assault machete" to kill two people and critically wound eleven more, so understandably people get a bit touchy when they see a bunch of autists whacking each other with swords in a public space. It's pretty difficult to make fair laws for this shit though - one side argues that it's a bit ridiculous when the police cracks down on LARPers, medieval reenactors and martial artists transporting their equipment, the other side argues that if you're too lenient bad actors will abuse the situation and carry bladed weapons for violent purposes. Now, the compromise is that we're allowed to do our shit as long as we coordinate with city hall, but someone just carrying a spear in the inner city for no reason would be apprehended real quick. Remember, we Eurofags generally aren't allowed to carry force multipliers for self defense (here in NL carrying a clawhammer on your toolbelt because you're a carpenter is okay, carrying a clawhammer in your bag because you're walking home at night through a shitty area is illegal and will get you fined if you're caught) so the only valid reasons to carry a spear publicly are membership in a martial arts club or reenacting.
